title: OGA validation plan
description: The structured artifact a learner produces for THEIR OWN target during the interactive workshop. It encodes the framework's 7-item checklist (10_validation_framework.md §5). It is simultaneously the learning artifact, the assessment input for the rubric, and the evidence recorded behind a workshop certificate. Designed to be analysable/shareable for the eLife 'intervention' write-up, so keep fields structured.

target_gene.description: The protein/gene the plan is about (by value, e.g. 'SNCA'). Never a pipeline FK — cross-DB linkage is by value only.

sample_type.description: The actual sample: cell line, primary cells, human FFPE tissue, plasma, etc. (framework item 1). Controls must match this context.

question_type.description: What the scientific question requires of the antibody (framework item 2 / §1). Drives how much evidence is needed.

question_statement.description: One sentence: what the learner is trying to show.

evidence_search.description: What existing evidence was found or not found, and where (framework item 3 / §4).

sources_checked.description: Must include at least one real source; OGA lookups should be grounded via Server A (target_report / antibody_validation).

found_genetic_validation.description: Whether knockout/knockdown-controlled evidence was found for the chosen antibody in this application/sample type.

notes.description: What the images/data actually showed (read images, not tick-boxes).

controls.description: The positive and negative control strategy (framework item 4 / §2, Module 20). This is the crux the rubric grades hardest.

positive.description: At least one control that DEFINES/ADDS the target (overexpression lysate, transfection, knock-in, KO-WT pair).

negative.description: At least one control that REMOVES/REDUCES the target (KO, knockdown, non-expressing line).

how_matched.description: How closely the controls match the experimental sample and assay (same cell type? same fixation? same protocol?).

antibody_identity.description: Full antibody identity (framework item 5). Enables reproducibility and RRID lookup via Server A.

orthogonal_readouts.description: Antibody-independent corroboration planned (framework item 6): RT-qPCR, RNA-seq, mass spec, etc.

decision.description: The documented decision (framework item 7). For a plan (pre-validation) this is the intended next step; the Recorder captures the post-validation outcome.

kind.description: The control TYPE. The rubric classifies each as selectivity-establishing or not (Module 20).

material.description: The specific reagent/line and its source.

why.description: Why this control answers (or supports) the selectivity question for this experiment.

rubric.description: How the tutor grades a plan before a workshop certificate can be claimed. Pass requires ALL hard gates. The reasoning checks are open-ended and LLM-graded against the framework; issuance is audited and bound to a verified institutional email.

hard_gates.check: question_type is set and the required evidence level is consistent with it (target_specific -> genetic-controlled evidence expected or a justified best-available fallback).
controls.positive contains at least one entry whose kind is in selectivity_control_kinds.
hard_gates.outcome: Learner chose a positive control that DEFINES the target.

hard_gates.check: controls.negative contains at least one entry whose kind is in selectivity_control_kinds (ideally knockout/knockdown, or a justified fallback).
hard_gates.outcome: Learner chose a negative control that REMOVES/REDUCES the target.

hard_gates.check: The learner does NOT rely on a non_selectivity_control_kind (peptide_block / isotype / secondary_only / loading_control) as their SELECTIVITY evidence. Such controls are fine to list as background/loading controls, but must not be offered as proof the signal is the target.
hard_gates.outcome: The sharpest learning outcome (Module 20) is demonstrated. This is the gate the exercise exists to teach.

hard_gates.check: evidence_search.sources_checked is non-empty and includes a real check (OGA lookups grounded via Server A). Absence of OGA data is acknowledged as non-verdict, not treated as failure.
hard_gates.outcome: Framework §4 understood; evidence is grounded, not invented.

hard_gates.check: decision is set with a rationale, and antibody_identity is sufficiently complete to be reproducible.

reasoning_checks: Can the learner say WHY their negative control answers 'is the signal my protein?' where an isotype control does not?

Do they prefer the target at ENDOGENOUS/relevant levels (an expressing cell of interest paired with a KO/KD in that same cell) over overexpression — and can they say when overexpression IS appropriate (screening/ruling out antibodies, or targets hard to express at relevant levels, ideally level-controlled e.g. lentiviral)?
Can they name a feasible fallback if their gold-standard control isn't available, with its caveat?
Do they articulate the throughline — that the controls they make (e.g. a knockdown) double as research tools for studying the target, so the reagents feed the rest of the work?
